newsitem.title: UK: World oil prices come off boil, still simmering.
newsitem.headline: World oil prices come off boil, still simmering.

text.p: World oil prices eased on Thursday as traders took profits from a rally which touched a five-year high last week.
Traders said a weak gasoline market helped drag crude oil lower, counteracting pressure from heating oil prices which were strong on low inventories in the United States and Europe.
November futures for benchmark Brent Blend crude stood at $21.96 per barrel by 1705 GMT, 35 cents down on the day but still $2.00 above where they stood at the end of August.
"There is no strength in gasoline and that's leading prices lower," said Alastair Harris of brokers MeesPierson.
"There is still upside risk with the tension in the Gulf and the underlying strength of heating oil," he added.

Concern about low heating oil stocks in the United States and Europe has kept prices simmering all year, and last week's military tension between the U.S. and Iraq brought the market to boiling point, driving Brent up to a five-year high of $24.39.
Dealers said Thursday's modest slide was a small correction in Brent's rise which has seen 1996 prices average $3 per barrel above last year.

The price spike is a bonanza for oil producing countries and oil companies, but it bodes ill for the big importers who face bigger fuel bills and even added inflationary pressures on their economies this winter.
The world's biggest oil producer, Saudi Arabia, could unexpectedly wipe out this year's entire $4.9 billion budget deficit, economists in the region said.
Even oil refiners saw a rise in profit margins, having weathered two years of low profitability, analysts said.

"As we came out of last winter, there was a risk of low gas oil stocks in the Atlantic as we began this winter, and this came to pass. This could be a source of margin upside in the fourth quarter," said an economist at a major European oil company.
But he added, "German consumer stocks are still low. They might end up regretting they didn't stock up earlier."
